One of the early web application vulnerabilities I remember was CVE-2000-0411 [CVE]. This was a simple vulnerability in a CGI-bin script used to send e-mail. The vulnerability was pretty straightforward: Adding additional parameters to the URL leaked environment variables. Other vulnerabilities allowed setting the "To" address and were heavily abused by spammers. And if parameters were passed directly to the sendmail binary, similar vulnerabilities could allow arbitrary code execution.



Source: SANS Internet Storm Center  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 6d

item.title: 🔵 Critical Rails Flaw Lets Attackers Write Server Files via Crafted ImageMagick Uploads
item.description:
Why this matters: Useful IT context for operational and leadership awareness.
A critical flaw in Ruby on Rails could allow an unauthenticated attacker to write arbitrary files on an app's server by uploading a crafted file if the app processes uploads using ImageMagick. item.title: 🟠 Xen Hypervisor Flaws Let One Malicious VM Read and Write Any Other VM's Memory
item.description:
Why this matters: Hospitality-system impact — consider guest services, PMS/POS, and property operations.
Two flaws in the Xen hypervisor allow a malicious guest virtual machine (VM) to read and write the memory of other VMs on the same host, including dom0. Dom0 is the VM that, by default, has full permissions and manages the others. Patches are out, and there is no known mitigation, the Xen Project said in an advisory on November 3.
